corrections.lexists_not_exists: `exists` follows the final link, so a DANGLING `instance.json` link read as absent and was then overwritten -- through the link, into wherever it pointed. Existing entries are detected without being followed, and any link at an owned name is refused outright.
corrections.one_admission_is_carried_not_repeated: `main` admitted, threw the answer away, and `install` admitted again -- so a source changed while `prepare` was composing was re-admitted and installed, exit 0, with a digest nobody had agreed to. `install` takes the admission it was given, refuses an admission made for another destination, and refuses a source that has drifted since.
corrections.owned_paths_are_decided_before_any_effec: install SUCCEEDED with an owned path linked outside the destination and published a selector `instance.read` rejected on the very next read -- a deployment that could never be started, left behind. `admit` now applies the same containment rule to every derived path BEFORE any effect.
corrections.the_native_validator_is_anchored_to_what: the first correction anchored `native_rpds` to the identity's OWN reported `resources`, so `resources: "/"` made every path on the host qualify and a prefix fallback admitted a file that was not in the manifest or did not exist. It is anchored to the admitted distro and its manifest entries; the permissive prefix fallback is gone.

reversal_probes.method: each probe proves a PASSING BASELINE on pristine code, reverts one guard in an isolated COPY of the tree, and requires the named checks to fail ON THE INTENDED ASSERTION [J1]
reversal_probes.one_arm_is_NOT_independently_reachable_a: the containment arm of the owned-path preflight cannot be reached without the link arm firing first, because every path `instance.layout` derives is a DIRECT child of the destination and a direct child only resolves outside by being a link. Probe K3-b therefore reverts the whole preflight rather than claiming to isolate that arm. The arm is kept because it is the invariant `instance.read` applies afterwards, and a layout that ever nests a path would reach it -- but it is belt-and-braces today and is reported as such rather than as covered.
reversal_probes.two_probes_first_PROVED_NOTHING_and_why: K3-c and K3-e failed on an assertion other than the one I had named. Reverted, the anchoring ADMITS the host path, so the intended failure is the refusal that never came, not the message it would have carried; and reverted, the drift is caught LATER by the copied-runtime comparison, so the intended failure is that the refusal names the wrong thing -- after a destination has been created and a distro copied, which is exactly the cost the earlier gate avoids. The probes were corrected to name those assertions rather than counted.
